title: Interleaved generator-to-WebStream adapter: resumable retries, backpressure and boundary integrity
creator: Anika Rao
description: Implement a production-ready adapter that safely bridges TypeScript async generators (AsyncGenerator / AsyncIterable) used by the SDK and the browser/node Web Streams API so callers can consume from either surface with predictable semantics. Current gaps: partial-consume cancellation semantics leak, retrying mid-stream can duplicate tokens or drop fragments, backpressure isn't honored consistently between sink/consumer orientations, and boundary integrity (token chunk boundaries, function-call frames) is fragile during resume. This ticket designs and implements a 'generator-proxy' adapter pattern with checkpointed resume tokens, idempotent fragment tagging, and an orthogonal backpressure handshake compatible with both ReadableStream default queuing and AsyncIterator pull semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes two ergonomic constructors: fromAsyncGenerator(generator, options) and toReadableStream(asyncGenerator, options)
Cancellation semantics: abort signals stop the source and close the stream without leaking resources (node/deno/browser tested)
Resumable retries: adapter emits compact checkpoint tokens at chunk/frame boundaries that allow the server/client to resume idempotently without duplicating previously delivered tokens
Backpressure: when consumer slows, adapter stops pulling from underlying runtime batching queue within 50ms on average (measured in benchmarks)
Boundary integrity: function-call frames and structured JSON outputs are preserved across adapter boundaries (no mid-frame splits on resume)
Interop tests: end-to-end examples cover (a) AsyncGenerator consumer -> ReadableStream sink, (b) ReadableStream consumer -> AsyncIterator sink, and (c) dual-consumer demux patterns
Documentation: short cookbooks (2 examples) and a migration note for existing SDK users
Performance: median additional CPU overhead < 4% and memory overhead < 8% versus raw AsyncGenerator in microbenchmarks
implementation_notes: Design: introduce Fragment IDs and CheckpointTokens. Fragment ID = stable prefix-hash + monotonic counter per response. Checkpoint token summarizes last-complete-fragment ID + stream-version metadata.
Retry flow: on transient network error, client can replay from nearest checkpoint token. Server-side will de-duplicate by fragment ID; client-side adapter will drop fragments already seen.

Backpressure handshake: use a thin credit-based protocol layered on top of pull-based async iterator. For ReadableStream default queuing, adapter will set highWaterMark dynamically and pause pulls when pendingCredits == 0.
Abort handling: wire AbortSignal to generator.return() and to underlying runtime cancellation RPC. Ensure aggregated cleanup runs once per stream to avoid double-freeing caches.
Boundary handling: prefer to buffer until complete syntactic units (JSON parseable chunk or function-call frame) before exposing to consumer; expose partial-chunk API opt-in for low-latency users.
Polyfills: add a lightweight helper for older Node versions that lack WHATWG ReadableStream semantics. Ship as separate module in SDK exports for tree-shaking.
Type definitions: provide accurate generics for payload types and a discriminated union for control records (checkpoint, fragment, eos).
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff. Drafted adapter contract and shared RFC with SDK team. Identified major failure modes (duplicate tokens during resume, cancel leaks).
2026-03-02: Prototype: generator-proxy implemented. Basic interop tests passing for simple text stream in Node 18+. Observed duplication bug when server replays partial fragments.
2026-03-05: Added Fragment ID scheme and draining window to prototype. Local tests show dedup removes duplicates for single retry, but edge-case with concurrent consumers remains.
2026-03-09: Benchmarks: added microbench harness. Median added latency ~1.9ms per chunk at 64B chunks; CPU overhead 3.5% compared to baseline. Need to optimize memory churn in buffer frontier.
2026-03-12: Integration: verified ReadableStream -> AsyncIterator and AsyncIterator -> ReadableStream examples in browser and deno. Filed follow-up ENG-100100 for cross-process stream tracing.
2026-03-14: PR opened (see links). Addressing review comments: (a) make checkpoint tokens smaller (~32 bytes), (b) expose opt-out for fragment buffering for low-latency mode.
qa_plan: Unit tests for fragment generation, checkpoint encoding/decoding, and dedup logic (simulate replays and partial replays)
Cross-runtime smoke tests: Chrome, Node 18/20, Deno latest. Validate AbortSignal flows and generator.return() behavior.
Fuzz tests: random chunk boundary splits to ensure buffer frontier preserves syntactic units and no JSON errors emitted to consumers
Integration tests: reconcile SDK consumer metrics (latency, dropped fragments) against a controlled server simulator that can inject failures
Load tests: 1000 concurrent streams with two retry events each to validate memory and CPU ceilings
rollout_plan: Canary release in next ts-sdk patch (ts-sdk-2026.04-canary). Enable adapter behind feature flag 'streamAdapterV2' for 10% of SDK traffic in staging.
Monitor: per-stream duplicate rate, resume success rate, aborted-stream leaks. Alert if duplicate rate > 0.5% or leaks increase vs baseline by 20%.
After 72h canary with green metrics, ramp to 50% then 100% over the following week. Communicate migration guide to developer-experience and support.
Fallback: if we observe persistent duplication on a particular customer workload, provide rollback and one-off patch to opt them out to buffering=false mode.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on checkpoint token size and privacy: tokens include no PII and are opaque to clients; confirm server-side dedup contract is acceptable.
Validate edge-case where consumer reads slowly for extended periods (>10s): ensure underlying runtime does not accumulate unbounded KV cache because of stalled streams.
API ergonomics: read the example snippets in PR and consider whether default should be buffering=true or low-latency=false for most users.
